<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:main}
$\mu(\zeta(2))\le \dfrac{C_0+C_1}{C_0-\widetilde C_2}=5.0193783774690093995\ldots<5.0193784$,
with the constants of Table~\ref{tab:cert}.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
$\mu(\pi^2)<5.0193784$, and $\mu(\pi\sqrt d)<10.0387568$ for every positive rational $d$.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:whipple}
For every $n\ge0$, $q_n+\hat q_n=0$.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
Under the conditions $\beta_1=0$, $\beta_2=\alpha_4-\alpha_1$, $\beta_3=\alpha_4-\alpha_2$, the
finite sums $q_n$ and $\hat q_n$ are, up to sign, the terminating ${}_4F_3(1)$ and
${}_5F_4(1)$ series on the two sides of Whipple's transformation
\cite[(2.4.2.3)]{Sl}; this identification is \cite[Remark~5]{Z14}. With the normalisations of
Section~\ref{sec:constr} the identity reads $q_n=-\hat q_n$. (This sign is confirmed in exact
arithmetic for $0\le n\le10$; see the ancillary file \texttt{verify\_\allowbreak zeta2\_\allowbreak exact.py}.)
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:refined}
Let $\hat a_3^*\le k<\hat b_2^*$ with $A_k\ne0$, and let $\mathcal N_k$ be the set of nonzero integers
$i-2k$ ($\hat b_0\le i<\hat a_0$), $i-k$ ($\hat b_1\le i<\hat a_1$), $i-k$ ($\hat a_2\le i<\hat b_2$, $i\ne k$),
$i-k$ ($\hat a_3\le i<\hat b_3$, $i\ne k$). Let $p$ be an odd prime with $p^2>\max_{c\in\mathcal N_k}|c|$,
and $\delta_k(p)=1$ if $p$ divides an element of $\mathcal N_k$, $\delta_k(p)=0$ otherwise. Then
\[
\operatorname{ord}_pB_k\ge\operatorname{ord}_pA_k-\delta_k(p).
\]
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Since $\hat a_3^*\le k<\hat b_2^*$, the factor $t+k$ occurs once in each of the two products of the
denominator of $\hat R$, and $G(t)=\hat R(t)(t+k)^2$ is a product of linear factors with
$G(-k)=A_k$ and $B_k=G'(-k)$. As $A_k\ne0$, no factor of the numerator vanishes at $t=-k$, and
\[
\frac{B_k}{A_k}=\frac{G'}{G}(-k)=\sum_{\hat b_0\le i<\hat a_0}\frac{2}{i-2k}+\sum_{\hat b_1\le i<\hat a_1}\frac1{i-k}
-\sum_{\substack{\hat a_2\le i<\hat b_2\\ i\ne k}}\frac1{i-k}-\sum_{\substack{\hat a_3\le i<\hat b_3\\ i\ne k}}\frac1{i-k}.
\]
Every denominator lies in $\mathcal N_k$; by the assumption on $p$ none is divisible by $p^2$,
and none is divisible by $p$ unless $\delta_k(p)=1$. Hence $\operatorname{ord}_p(B_k/A_k)\ge-\delta_k(p)$.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:den}
Let $\operatorname{den}(\xi)$ denote the denominator of $\xi\in\mathbb{Q}$. Then
$\limsup_n\frac1n\log\operatorname{den}(p_n+\hat p_n)\le K$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Let $c\ge\max\{\gamma_1,\hat c_1\}$ be a constant, depending only on the parameters, such that for $p>\sqrt{cn}$ every integer $L$ occurring as an argument of $\Lambda_s$ in \eqref{eq:phat} and every element of every set $\mathcal N_k$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:refined} is smaller than $p^2$ in absolute value. Since $D_{\gamma_1n}D_{\gamma_2n}p_n$ and
$D_{\hat c_1n}D_{\hat c_2n}\hat p_n$ are integers, the primes $p\le\sqrt{cn}$ contribute
$O(\sqrt n\log n)$ to $\log\operatorname{den}(p_n+\hat p_n)$. Let $p>\sqrt{cn}$ and $x=n/p$; then
$\operatorname{ord}_pD_{\gamma n}=\mathbf 1[p\le\gamma n]$ and
$\operatorname{ord}_p(p_n+\hat p_n)\ge\min\{\operatorname{ord}_pp_n,\operatorname{ord}_p\hat p_n\}$.

\emph{Primes $p>n$.} By \eqref{eq:lemma7}, $\operatorname{ord}_pp_n\ge-u_1(x)$. By \cite[(25)]{Z14},
$\operatorname{ord}_p\hat p_n\ge-e_2(x)$. In \eqref{eq:phat} we bound the terms one by one: $\operatorname{ord}_pA_k\ge
E_k(p)$ and, by \eqref{eq:24} and Lemma~\ref{lem:refined}, $\operatorname{ord}_pB_k\ge E_k(p)-\delta_k(p)$
when $\hat a_3^*\le k<\hat b_2^*$ and $A_k\ne0$, $\operatorname{ord}_pB_k\ge E_k(p)-1$ otherwise; moreover
$\operatorname{ord}_p\Lambda_2(L)\ge-2\cdot\mathbf 1[p\le L]$ and $\operatorname{ord}_p\Lambda_1(L)\ge-\mathbf 1[p\le L]$ since $p^2>L$.
Setting $y=(k-1)/p$ as in the proof of \cite[Lemma~8]{Z14}, these bounds become
$E-2\chi$, $E-1-\chi$ and $E-\delta-\chi$ at $(x,y)$ (the $A$-terms live on $J_1$, the
$B$-terms on $J_2$), up to a set of primes on which $x$ lies within $O(1/p)$ of one of finitely
many rational points; these contribute $o(n)$. Hence $\operatorname{ord}_p\hat p_n\ge-\min\{e_2(x),\upsilon(x)\}=-u_2(x)$
outside that set, and $\operatorname{ord}_p(p_n+\hat p_n)\ge-\max\{u_1,u_2\}(x)$.

\emph{Primes $\sqrt{cn}<p\le n$.} Here $e_1=e_2=2$ and, by \eqref{eq:lemma7} and
\cite[Lemma~8]{Z14}, $\operatorname{ord}_p(p_n+\hat p_n)\ge-2+\min\{\varphi,\hat\varphi\}(n/p)$.

By the prime number theorem, for a step function $w$ vanishing near $0$,
$\sum_{p>n}w(n/p)\log p=n\int_0^1w(x)\,dx/x^2+o(n)$ and, for $1$-periodic $w$,
$\sum_{\sqrt{cn}<p\le n}w(n/p)\log p=n\int_0^1w(\theta)\,d\psi(1+\theta)+o(n)$, since
$\psi'(1+\theta)=\sum_{k\ge1}(k+\theta)^{-2}$ (this is the standard computation behind \cite[Lemma~7]{Z14}). With $\psi(2)-\psi(1)=1$ this
gives the bound $K$.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:decay}
For $\sigma_0=-32.2134$ one has $\limsup_n\frac1n\log|\hat r_n|\le\sup_{y\in\mathbb{R}}\hat H(y)\le-299.1530<-K-1$.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
The interval $(-\hat\alpha_0^*/2,-\hat\beta_0/2)=(-77,-15.5)$ contains $\sigma_0$, so for large $n$ there is
$c_n\in\frac12\mathbb{Z}+\frac14$ with $|c_n-n\sigma_0|\le\frac14$ inside the strip
$-\hat a_0^*/2<\operatorname{Re}t<(1-\hat b_0)/2$, in which the integrand of $\hat r_n$ is holomorphic
(the poles of $\pi/\sin2\pi t$ there are cancelled by zeros of $\hat R$, \cite[\S6]{Z14}); we
move the contour to $\operatorname{Re}t=c_n$. On it, $|\pi/\sin2\pi t|=\pi/\cosh(2\pi\operatorname{Im}t)$.
On this line $\operatorname{Re}(2t+\hat b_0)$ and $\operatorname{Re}(t+\hat b_1)$ are negative; we use
$1/\Gamma(z)=\Gamma(1-z)\sin(\pi z)/\pi$ and $|\sin\pi z|\le e^{\pi|\operatorname{Im}z|}$ for
these two factors. The eight Gamma factors then have arguments $nw+O(1)$, $w=k\tau+c$,
$(\epsilon,k,c)\in\Sigma$, $\tau=\sigma_0+iy$, $y=\operatorname{Im}t/n$, all with
$\operatorname{Re}w\ge21.78$. Stirling's formula, applied to them and to the four factorials of
the normalising constant, gives
$\log|\hat R(t)\pi/\sin2\pi t|\le n\hat H(y)+O(\log(n+|\operatorname{Im}t|))$ uniformly on the
line: the terms in $n\log n$ and in $n$ cancel because $\sum\hat\alpha_j=\sum\hat\beta_j$, and the
exponential factors give $e^{\pi n(2|y|+|y|-2|y|)}=e^{\pi n|y|}$. For $|y|$ large,
$\hat H(y)=-2\pi|y|+(\hat\alpha_0-\hat\beta_0)\log2+h_\Pi+O(y^{-2})$, so the integral over the line is
$\le e^{n\sup\hat H+O(\log n)}$. The numerical bound is certified (file \texttt{verify\_\allowbreak zeta2.py}):
$\hat H$ is even; on $[0,2000]$ it is enclosed by $47$ Arb balls, the largest upper bound being
$-299.15302$; for $y\ge2000$,
$\hat H(y)\le-2\pi y+(\hat\alpha_0-\hat\beta_0)\log2+h_\Pi+\sum_{\Sigma}\frac{(\operatorname{Re}w)^3}{2k^2y^2}<-12472$.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
At the non-real critical point $\hat\tau_0$ of the second construction (a root of
$(2\tau+\hat\alpha_0)^2\prod_{j=1}^3(\tau+\hat\alpha_j)-(2\tau+\hat\beta_0)^2\prod_{j=1}^3(\tau+\hat\beta_j)$,
$\hat\tau_0=-32.21344848\ldots\pm14.37727696\ldots i$), taking $\sigma_0=\operatorname{Re}\hat\tau_0$ one finds $\hat H(\operatorname{Im}\hat\tau_0)=-325.4478457713\ldots=-C_0$ to all computed
digits, as Theorem~\ref{thm:coinc} predicts.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:coinc}
With the parameters \eqref{eq:param}--\eqref{eq:hatparam}, $r_n+\hat r_n=0$ for all
sufficiently large $n$; that is, $q_n=-\hat q_n$ and $p_n=-\hat p_n$.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
By Lemma~\ref{lem:whipple}, $\Delta_n:=r_n+\hat r_n=-(p_n+\hat p_n)\in\mathbb{Q}$. By
\cite[Lemma~6]{Z14} and Lemma~\ref{lem:decay},
$|\Delta_n|\le|r_n|+|\hat r_n|\le e^{(-\min\{C_0,K+1\}+o(1))n}$, and by Lemma~\ref{lem:den},
$\operatorname{den}(\Delta_n)\le e^{(K+o(1))n}$. Since $C_0-K=31.4070\ldots>0$ (Table~\ref{tab:cert}),
$|\operatorname{den}(\Delta_n)\Delta_n|<1$ for large $n$; this is an integer, so $\Delta_n=0$.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
For the smaller parameters $(19,16,13,22;\,0,3,6,38)$ the same proof gives
$\mu(\zeta(2))\le5.0204524708476832909\ldots$, with $C_0=42.33438299777\ldots$,
$K=38.31605710342\ldots$, $C_0-K=4.01832589434\ldots$ and $\sup\hat H\le-39.3547$ on
$\operatorname{Re}\tau=-4.1774$; this instance is quicker to verify and is also treated by the
ancillary files.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
